problem: Share record fingerprints across Python and JavaScript without formatting, key-order, or numeric-spelling drift inside the declared numeric domain.

outputs.representation: RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 bytes and SHA-256 receipt

numeric_profile: Binary64 finite numbers. Reject integral values outside +/-9007199254740991 in every spelling; reject nonzero underflow. Larger/exact-decimal identifiers must be strings.

criteria.claim: Match all 26 published RFC Appendix B number examples, including the two required rejections.
Match the published UTF-16 sorting example and canonical UTF-8 sample.
Reject duplicate keys, invalid Unicode, nonfinite/unsafe numbers and non-object roots.
Equal admitted records have equal canonical bytes and digests after formatting/key-order changes; preserve array order and string distinctions.
Produce a source/contract-bound sidecar without changing legacy internal evidence IDs.

limitations: This is a strict subset of accepted JCS inputs, not a parser accepting all JSON numbers.
Numeric decimal rounding follows binary64; it is not exact decimal arithmetic.
No Unicode normalization, unit conversion, schema truth check, signature or ownership proof.
No automatic source replacement, migration, market claim or deployment.
